prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity desktop portfolio landing-page direction comp, 1536 by 1024 landscape
Primary request: Design the conventional category-standard personal portfolio for COLTON SPURGIN, executed with excellent hierarchy, spacing, accessibility, and restraint. The visitor must understand who Colton is and scan his work quickly.
Scene/backdrop: no scene; flat front-facing website screenshot
Subject: a polished personal portfolio for an Air Force NCO, lead software developer intern, research assistant, and UWF senior specializing in AI who graduates December 2026
Style/medium: high-fidelity contemporary editorial web UI, clean neutral grid, sober professional tone
Composition/framing: top navigation with COLTON SPURGIN left and WORK, EXPERIENCE, ABOUT, CONTACT right; left-aligned hero headline “SOFTWARE DEVELOPER, AIR FORCE NCO, AND AI RESEARCHER.” with a short factual introduction and VIEW THE WORK button; below it, a familiar four-card SELECTED WORK grid labeled BORK, VELLM, TSP BENCHMARKS, HOME LAB; show the beginning of a clean EXPERIENCE timeline. Use typography and spacing as the main craft.
Color palette: white #ffffff, ink #111827, blue #2563eb, gray #64748b
Materials/textures: clean grid, restrained project screenshot placeholders, hairline rules
Text (verbatim): “COLTON SPURGIN”; “WORK”; “EXPERIENCE”; “ABOUT”; “CONTACT”; “SOFTWARE DEVELOPER, AIR FORCE NCO, AND AI RESEARCHER.”; “I build useful software, study AI at UWF, and bring military leadership to technical work.”; “VIEW THE WORK”; “SELECTED WORK”; “BORK”; “VELLM”; “TSP BENCHMARKS”; “HOME LAB”; “EXPERIENCE”
Constraints: unmistakably a usable desktop website; exact conventional portfolio pattern; polished and accessible; no logo; no invented employers, metrics, awards, testimonials, or project claims
Avoid: conceptual metaphor, experimental navigation, neon cyber aesthetic, bento grid, 3D mockup, browser chrome, illegible pseudo-text, gradients, excessive rounded cards, watermark
